note.text: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level. A consumer-price measure tracks a defined basket with weights reflecting a specified method. An individual price can rise while others fall, so its movement alone does not establish general inflation. Calculate a period’s percentage index change using the earlier index as denominator. A change in index points is not automatically the same numerical percentage. The fictional indices here teach arithmetic; they are not current Cameroon inflation statistics.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to calculate a price-index change and distinguish general inflation from a single price movement. Builds on: basket records, indices and purchasing power. Leads to: causes, effects and the distinction from deflation.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Original index: {120} rises to {126}. The change is {126-120} index points, while the percentage change is {100*(126-120)/120}%. A stationery price alone cannot establish that all national prices rose at that rate. Nor does a lower inflation rate necessarily mean falling prices.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the periods and index method, subtract earlier from later and divide by earlier before multiplying by {100}. Label percentage and index points separately. Check whether the evidence describes one item or a broader price measure.

cards.idea: Distinguish the monetary concepts before evaluating a case.
example: inflation: a sustained increase in the general price level.

percentage inflation rate: The earlier level is the reference for this change.
